claim: H3K64ac is an uncharacterized acetylation site on histone H3 lysine 64 identified by mass spectrometry.
source: We used mass spectrometry to identify novel histone modifications and found an uncharacterized acetylation site on histone H3 lysine 64 (H3K64ac) (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: Supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1A and supplementary figures, demonstrating detection of acetylated K64 peptides.

claim: H3K64 is located on the lateral surface of the histone octamer in close proximity to the inner gyre of DNA.
source: H3K64 is the first amino acid of the H3 alpha1 helix, the first of three alpha helices in the histone fold. It is found on the lateral surface of the histone octamer in close proximity to the inner gyre of DNA (Davey et al., 2002; Figure 1B) at a location distinct from other potentially acetylated residues, such as H3K56.
evidence: Supported by structural data from Davey et al., 2002 and 3D modeling shown in Figure 1B.

claim: H3K64ac is present in a variety of mouse and human cell lines and tissues.
source: Using this antibody, we found that H3K64ac is present in a variety of mouse and human cell lines and tissues suggesting a rather ubiquitous function (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2I).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data showing H3K64ac detection across multiple cell lines in Figure 1D and supplementary figures.

claim: H3K64 acetylation levels increase upon HDAC-inhibitor treatment.
source: Upon HDAC-inhibitor treatment, H3K64 acetylation levels increased (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2I).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data comparing untreated and Na-butyrate treated cells.

claim: H3K64ac shows a distinct nuclear localization with relative depletion from heterochromatin.
source: Immunofluorescence (IF) showed a distinct nuclear localization of H3K64ac with a relative depletion from heterochromatin (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 3, compare panels 5 and 6, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2H).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence imaging showing H3K64ac distribution pattern in cells.

claim: The localization pattern of H3K64ac is opposite to that of H3K64me3.
source: Interestingly, this localization pattern is the opposite to that of H3K64me3 (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by comparative immunofluorescence data showing mutually exclusive localization patterns.

claim: H3K64me3 is a repressive mark enriched in pericentromeric heterochromatin.
source: We previously established that H3K64me3 is a novel repressive mark enriched in pericentromeric heterochromatin that might help to 'lock' the conformation and/or position of the nucleosome, and consequently the surrounding chromatin (Daujat et al., 2009; Lange et al., 2013)
evidence: Supported by previous publications from the authors' group.

claim: H3K64ac is strongly enriched at the transcriptional start site (TSS) of active genes.
source: In line with the euchromatic localization detected in IF, we found strong enrichment of H3K64ac at the transcriptional start site (TSS) of active genes (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: Supported by ChIP-on-chip data showing H3K64ac enrichment at active TSSs.

claim: H3K64ac enrichment at TSSs shows strong correlation with RNA Polymerase II occupancy.
source: At TSSs, we detected a strong correlation between the enrichment of H3K64ac and RNA Polymerase II occupancy (Figure 2B), as well as with the presence of active histone marks (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), suggesting a role for H3K64ac in transcriptional activation.
evidence: Supported by scatterplot analysis showing correlation between H3K64ac and RNA Pol II ChIP data.

claim: Local H3K64ac enrichment is indicative of the steady-state mRNA level of the respective gene.
source: Of note, local H3K64ac enrichment is indicative of the steady-state mRNA level of the respective gene (Figure 2C) and it is not simply due to increased histone H3 density (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Supported by meta-gene plot analysis correlating H3K64ac levels with gene expression levels.

claim: H3K64ac enrichment is anti-correlated with repressive marks such as H3K27me3 and H3K64me3.
source: Consistent with this, H3K64ac enrichment is anti-correlated with repressive marks such as H3K27me3 and H3K64me3 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by scatterplot analysis showing negative correlation between H3K64ac and repressive marks.

claim: H3K64ac is strongly enriched at enhancers, with a preference for active enhancers.
source: Furthermore, we find H3K64ac strongly enriched at enhancers (Figure 2A), with a preference for active enhancers, where it co-localizes with established enhancer marks such as H3K27ac, H3K4me1, and p300-binding (Figure 2D; Creyghton et al., 2010; Rada-Iglesias et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by ChIP-on-chip data and comparison with published enhancer datasets.

claim: H3K64ac levels are very low at repetitive elements where H3K64me3 is highly enriched.
source: Multiple single gene validations by ChIP-qPCR confirmed the genome-wide data and also revealed that H3K64ac levels are very low at repetitive elements (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B), where H3K64me3 is highly enriched (Daujat et al., 2009), again indicating opposing genomic localizations for these two marks.
evidence: Supported by ChIP-qPCR data at repetitive elements and previous publication on H3K64me3.

claim: H3K64ac enrichment shifts from pluripotency-associated genes to differentiation-associated genes during ES cell differentiation.
source: In pluripotent ES cells, H3K64ac is strongly enriched at active pluripotency-associated genes such as Nanog, Pou5f1 and Dppa3, whereas after retinoic acid-induced differentiation this enrichment shifts towards active differentiation-associated genes (e.g., Hoxb3 and Hoxd3, Pax6) demonstrating that H3K64ac levels reflect transcriptional activity during differentiation.
evidence: Supported by ChIP analysis comparing undifferentiated and differentiated ES cells shown in Figure 3A.

claim: H3K64ac is most highly enriched on the H3 variant H3.3.
source: In line with previous findings that H3.3 has covalent modifications associated with transcriptionally active chromatin (Hake et al., 2006), we found the highest enrichment of H3K64ac on the H3 variant H3.3 (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by immunoprecipitation data of Flag-HA-tagged H3 variants showing highest H3K64ac signal on H3.3.

claim: The transcriptionally active alleles of imprinting control regions (ICRs) are specifically marked by H3K64ac.
source: We analysed five imprinting control regions (ICRs) and in each case we found that the transcriptionally active alleles were specifically enriched in H3K64ac, whereas the inactive ones were enriched in H3K64me3 (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by allele-specific ChIP data using polymorphic nucleotides to distinguish parental alleles.

claim: H3K64ac and H3K64me3 can define functionally opposing chromatin states.
source: These data suggest that H3K64ac and H3K64me3 can define functionally opposing chromatin states.
evidence: Inferred from the mutually exclusive distribution patterns and opposing associations with active vs. inactive chromatin.

claim: Knockdown of p300 and CBP decreases the steady-state levels of H3K64ac.
source: In these assays, knockdown of p300 and CBP, but not of other HATs decreased the steady-state levels of H3K64ac (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by siRNA knockdown experiments followed by immunoblot analysis.

claim: The decrease in H3K64ac upon p300/CBP knockdown is most pronounced at p300/CBP-specific genomic target regions.
source: This decrease was most pronounced at p300/CBP-specific genomic target regions (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by ChIP-qPCR analysis at specific genomic loci following p300/CBP knockdown.

claim: Overexpression of p300 results in increased levels of H3K64ac.
source: In line with this, overexpression of p300 resulted in increased levels of H3K64ac (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), and p300 and H3K64ac distributions showed a strong correlation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data showing increased H3K64ac in p300-overexpressing cells.

claim: p300 and CBP can acetylate H3K64 in vitro on free H3 and within chromatin.
source: Moreover, p300 and CBP can acetylate H3K64 in vitro on free H3 (Figure 4D) and within chromatin (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by in vitro HAT assays using recombinant H3 and chromatin templates.

claim: p300/CBP are H3K64 acetyltransferases.
source: Altogether these data clearly establish p300/CBP as H3K64 acetyltransferases, not excluding the presence of additional H3K64 acetyltransferases.
evidence: Inferred from multiple lines of evidence including knockdown, overexpression, and in vitro acetylation assays.

claim: Chd1 repositions H3K64-acetylated nucleosomes faster than unmodified nucleosomes.
source: Our results show that Chd1 repositioned H3K64-acetylated nucleosomes faster than unmodified nucleosomes. This was not the case when we used the RSC enzyme (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by in vitro chromatin remodeling assays comparing rates of nucleosome repositioning.

claim: Acetylation of H3K64 differentially affects chromatin remodeling enzymes.
source: This suggests that acetylation of H3K64 could differentially affect remodelling enzymes.
evidence: Inferred from the differential effects observed with Chd1 vs. RSC remodeling enzymes.

claim: H3K64ac nucleosomes are more sensitive to salt-induced disruption than unmodified nucleosomes.
source: Using this strategy, we observed that the FRET interaction for H3K64ac nucleosomes was more sensitive to salt-disruption than unmodified nucleosomes at NaCl concentrations ranging between ∼0.5 M and 1.0 M (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by FRET measurements showing lower salt stability of H3K64ac nucleosomes.

claim: Single-molecule FRET measurements show lower stability of H3K64ac nucleosomes compared to unmodified nucleosomes.
source: In parallel, we also measured the salt-dependent nucleosome stability by single-molecule FRET, which again resulted in a lower stability of H3K64ac nucleosomes (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by single-molecule FRET data showing decreased nucleosome stability.

claim: H3K64ac decreases nucleosome stability, distinguishing it from H3K56ac which does not significantly affect nucleosome stability.
source: Together these data demonstrate a decreased stability of H3K64ac nucleosomes, distinguishing this acetylation from H3K56ac that was reported not to significantly affect nucleosome stability under comparable conditions (Neumann et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by comparison with published data on H3K56ac and current experimental results.

claim: H3K64ac reduces the level of nucleosome assembly relative to unmodified H3 in competitive reconstitution assays.
source: Figure 5B shows that H3K64ac reduces the level of nucleosome assembly, relative to unmodified H3, indicating that H3K64 acetylation reduces histone–DNA binding affinity.
evidence: Supported by competitive nucleosome assembly experiments showing reduced assembly efficiency.

claim: Acetylation at H3K9 has no detectable effect on nucleosome stability or assembly.
source: In contrast, acetylation at H3K9 had no detectable effect (Figure 5A,B), illustrating functional differences between acetylation of lateral surface and histone tail lysines.
evidence: Supported by FRET and competitive assembly data comparing H3K9ac to H3K64ac.

claim: H3K64ac directly influences histone–DNA association and nucleosome stability.
source: In concert, these observations demonstrate that H3K64ac directly influences histone–DNA association and nucleosome stability.
evidence: Inferred from multiple in vitro assays showing effects on nucleosome stability and assembly.

claim: H3K64ac levels dramatically increase in elongating spermatids during the period of nucleosome disassembly and histone replacement.
source: In spermatocytes and round spermatids H3K64ac was below the limit of detection. However, the levels of H3K64ac dramatically increased in elongating spermatids (Figure 5C,D). At approximately the same time, we also detected the presence of some specific H3 tail acetylations (Figure 5—figure supplement 4A). Notably, we observed this increase in H3K64ac precisely during the period of nucleosome disassembly and replacement of histones by transition proteins in spermiogenesis.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence and immunohistochemistry data on testis sections.

claim: H3K64ac may play a role in histone replacement during spermiogenesis by creating a less stable, more 'open' chromatin state.
source: Our present data suggest a potential role for lateral surface modifications, such as H3K64ac, in this replacement process by creating a less stable, more 'open' chromatin state.
evidence: Inferred from the timing of H3K64ac appearance during spermiogenesis and its known effects on nucleosome stability.

claim: H3K64me3 is enriched in regions of spermatids where genomic regions undergo late histone replacement.
source: In contrast to this, H3K64me3 is enriched in the part of the spermatid where genomic regions that undergo late histone replacement are located, suggesting that H3K64me3 may 'stabilize' particular regions of chromatin thereby protecting them from histone exchange (Figure 5—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data on testis sections showing H3K64me3 localization.

claim: H3K64ac promotes histone displacement from chromatin more than H3K64R in eviction assays.
source: Using this assay, we detected more H3 in the evicted fraction from H3K64ac chromatin than from H3K64R chromatin (Figure 6A, right panel, Figure 6—figure supplement 2A), suggesting that the destabilization introduced by H3K64ac facilitates histone displacement and eviction.
evidence: Supported by in vitro histone eviction assays comparing different H3 species.

claim: The observed difference in histone eviction is not due to differential Nap1 histone binding.
source: Of note, we detected equivalent binding of Nap1 to each of the H3 species used (unmodified, K64R, or K64ac) indicating that the observed difference in histone eviction is not due to differential Nap1 histone binding (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Supported by Nap1 pull-down experiments showing equal binding to all H3 species.

claim: The acetylation mimic H3K64Q promotes transcription of early-response genes c-fos, Egr1, and c-myc above levels obtained with wildtype H3.3 or H3.3K64R.
source: In this setup, H3K64Q promoted the expression of certain genes, such as c-fos, Egr1, and c-myc, (Figure 6B), above the levels obtained when assaying wildtype H3.3 or the acetylation-deficient H3.3K64R.
evidence: Supported by qPCR analysis of gene expression in NIH3T3 cells expressing different H3.3 variants.

claim: Expression of control genes Gapdh and Hsp70 is unaffected by H3K64Q.
source: Notably, expression of control genes such as Gapdh and Hsp70 was unaffected (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data showing no change in control gene expression.

claim: H3K64ac has an intrinsic ability to impact upon transcription mechanisms in vivo.
source: The observed transcriptional effects due to a single acetylation mimic within the globular domain strongly suggest that H3K64ac has an intrinsic ability to impact upon transcription mechanisms in vivo.
evidence: Inferred from the transcriptional effects observed with the H3K64Q acetylation mimic.

claim: The main chain atoms of H3K64 are in direct contact with the DNA phosphate backbone.
source: The main chain atoms of H3K64 are in direct contact with the DNA phosphate backbone and this places the H3K64 side chain close enough to potentially contact the DNA, with the average H3K64 side-chain nitrogen-to-DNA distance approximately 6.1 Å (Figure 5—figure supplement 5A,B).
evidence: Supported by structural analysis of the high-resolution nucleosome crystal structure.

claim: Lysine acetylation results in increased bulk and charge neutralization of the lysine side-chain.
source: Lysine acetylation results in increased bulk and charge neutralization of the lysine side-chain, and it is likely that acetylation of lateral surface lysines (e.g., H3K64) could interfere with histone–DNA interactions.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of the chemical effects of lysine acetylation.

claim: H3K64 is involved in an extensive network of water-mediated hydrogen bonds linking water molecules, histone atoms, and DNA.
source: Interestingly, in the high-resolution crystal structure of the nucleosome (PDB 1KX5; Davey et al., 2002) H3K64 is found to be involved in an extensive network of water-mediated hydrogen bonds that link numerous water molecules, histone side- and main-chain atoms and the DNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 5C).
evidence: Supported by analysis of the high-resolution nucleosome crystal structure from Davey et al., 2002.

claim: Acetylation of H3K64 would be predicted to disrupt the water-mediated hydrogen bond network.
source: Acetylation of H3K64 would be predicted to disrupt this hydrogen bond network.
evidence: Inferred from the structural position of H3K64 and the chemical effects of acetylation.

claim: Water-bridged interactions between histones and DNA are as important to nucleosome stability as direct histone–DNA contacts.
source: Davey et al. estimate from their crystallographic analysis that water-bridged interactions between histones and DNA are as important to nucleosome stability as the direct histone–DNA contacts (Davey et al., 2002).
evidence: Based on published crystallographic analysis by Davey et al., 2002.

claim: Disruption of even a single water-bridge interaction has the potential to significantly affect nucleosome stability.
source: They postulate that disruption of even a single water–bridge interaction (e.g., acetylation of H3K64) has the potential to significantly affect nucleosome stability. This is indeed fully supported by our findings—we demonstrate that H3K64ac exerts a direct effect on nucleosome stability and facilitates histone eviction.
evidence: Based on postulation by Davey et al. and supported by experimental findings in this study.

claim: The observed enrichment of H3K64ac at active gene promoters argues for a role in creating an open, permissive chromatin state.
source: Moreover, the observed enrichment of H3K64ac at active gene promoters and during chromatin reorganization in spermiogenesis argues for a role of H3K64ac in creating an open, permissive chromatin state.
evidence: Inferred from the genomic distribution patterns and functional context of H3K64ac.

claim: A twofold higher transcription due to a single histone mutation is considered biologically important.
source: We consider a twofold higher transcription due to a single histone mutation as biologically important.
evidence: This is a statement of the authors' interpretation of the biological significance of their findings.

claim: Different acetylations on the octamer's lateral surface can mediate distinct effects on nucleosomes.
source: Additional lysines on the octamer's lateral surface have been found to be acetylated, such as H3K56, which is located closer to the ends of the nucleosomal DNA. Interestingly, these acetylations can mediate distinct effects on nucleosomes (this work and Neumann et al., 2009; Tropberger et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by comparison with published work on H3K56ac and other lateral surface modifications.

claim: Specificity exists in the way that the biomechanical properties of nucleosomes are affected differentially by acetylation at different sites within the globular domain of H3.
source: Thus, specificity exists in the way that the biomechanical properties of nucleosomes are affected differentially by acetylation at different sites within the globular domain of H3.
evidence: Inferred from the distinct effects observed for different acetylation sites.

claim: H3K64ac might serve to prevent the nucleosome from adopting a repressive conformation, thereby maintaining chromatin in a transcriptionally competent state.
source: However, H3K64ac may also function by preventing H3K64me3 from being laid down at key genomic regions. We have previously suggested that methylation of H3K64 is involved in the creation of repressive chromatin states (Daujat et al., 2009; Lange et al., 2013). Thus, H3K64ac might serve to prevent the nucleosome from adopting a repressive conformation, thereby maintaining chromatin in a transcriptionally competent state.
evidence: Inferred from the mutually exclusive distribution of H3K64ac and H3K64me3 and their opposing functions.

claim: Opposing chromatin states can be defined via the mutually exclusive presence of H3K64ac or H3K64me3.
source: Our working model (Figure 7) proposes that opposing chromatin states can be defined via the mutually exclusive presence of H3K64ac or H3K64me3. This model is reinforced by the observed distinct and largely mutually exclusive genomic distribution patterns of these two H3K64 modifications.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the cumulative evidence from genomic distribution and functional studies.

claim: Lateral surface modifications play a key role in regulating chromatin function.
source: The data provided here strengthen the concept that lateral surface modifications play a key role in regulating chromatin function, as initially proposed by others (Cosgrove et al., 2004; Mersfelder and Parthun, 2006) and us (Tropberger and Schneider, 2013).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the current study and supported by previous publications.

claim: The identification of novel pathways regulating chromatin function has the potential to highlight druggable targets for diseases in which chromatin states have been distorted.
source: The identification of novel pathways regulating chromatin function has also the potential to highlight druggable targets for diseases in which chromatin states have been distorted.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential therapeutic applications.

claim: H3K64ac regulates nucleosome stability and facilitates nucleosome eviction and gene expression in vivo.
source: We show that H3K64ac regulates nucleosome stability and facilitates nucleosome eviction and hence gene expression in vivo.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by multiple lines of evidence throughout the manuscript.

claim: H3K64ac defines transcriptionally active chromatin.
source: In line with this, we demonstrate that H3K64ac is enriched in vivo at the transcriptional start sites of active genes and it defines transcriptionally active chromatin.
evidence: Supported by ChIP-on-chip data showing enrichment at active TSSs and correlation with transcriptional activity.

claim: H3K64ac opposes its repressive counterpart H3K64me3.
source: Moreover, we find that the p300 co-activator acetylates H3K64, and consistent with a transcriptional activation function, H3K64ac opposes its repressive counterpart H3K64me3.
evidence: Supported by the mutually exclusive distribution patterns and opposing functional associations.

claim: Lateral surface modifications can define functionally opposing chromatin states.
source: Our findings reveal an important role for a histone modification within the nucleosome core as a regulator of chromatin function and they demonstrate that lateral surface modifications can define functionally opposing chromatin states.
evidence: This is a major conclusion of the study based on the opposing functions of H3K64ac and H3K64me3.
